atAGlance: Nem cuốn is fresh nem rolls, usually with rice paper, herbs, noodles, pork or shrimp depending on the shop, and peanut-hoisin dip or fish-sauce-lime dip.
whatItIs: Nem cuốn is a cool rice-paper roll with herbs, noodles, and pork or shrimp depending on the shop. Peanut-hoisin dip makes it rich; fish-sauce dip makes it lighter and sharper.
howToEnjoy: Eat nem cuốn fresh, before the herbs wilt and the rice paper dries. Dip each bite lightly so the roll stays clean and bright.
howLocalsOrder: Order nem cuốn by the plate or by the roll, then ask which dip comes with it. If peanuts are a problem, ask for no peanuts before the dip arrives.
worthKnowing: Across Vietnam, nem cuốn can overlap with fresh-roll language in different regions, so the filling and dip matter more than the English translation.
goodToKnow: If peanut-hoisin dip or fish-sauce-lime dip comes separately, start with a small dip; it can be salty, sweet, sour, and spicy at once.
